messages.text: Williams sisters given wild card for US Open women's doubles

metadata.summary: Serena and Venus Williams will play together in the 2026 US Open women's doubles after being given a wild card to enter the tournament.
metadata.content: Serena and Venus Williams given wild card to compete in 2026 US Open women's doubles tournament | Tennis News | Sky Sports Skip to content Breaking Serena and Venus Williams given wild card to compete in 2026 US Open women's doubles tournament Serena and Venus Williams to play doubles together at a Grand Slam for the first time since the 2022 US Open; Serena played in mixed doubles alongside Carlos Alcaraz on Tuesday; watch the 2026 US Open live on Sky Sports Tennis and Sky Sports+, NOW and the Sky Sports app Wednesday 26 August 2026 15:29, UK Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Highlights of Serena and Venus Williams against Marta Kostyuk and Peyton Stearns from the Cincinnati Open. Serena and Venus Williams will play together in the 2026 US Open women's doubles after being given a wild card to enter the tournament. The sisters played competitively together for the first time since the 2022 US Open at the Cincinnati Open earlier this month, and will now return to Grand Slam action at the scene of their last major outing as a pair. Serena made a sensational return to tennis during the grass-court season after almost four years out of the professional game, but the 44-year-old suffered a knee injury during a first-round singles loss which led to her and Venus withdrawing from the doubles at the All England Club. metadata.summary: Solheim Cup captain Anna Nordqvist has announced via social media that she will retire from playing professional golf after this week's FM Championship, live on Sky Sports.
metadata.content: Anna Nordqvist: Team Europe's Solheim Cup captain announces shock mid-season retirement from playing professional golf | Golf News | Sky Sports Skip to content Anna Nordqvist: Team Europe's Solheim Cup captain announces shock mid-season retirement from playing professional golf Three-time major winner and nine-time Solheim Cup player Anna Nordqvist will retire from playing professional golf at the FM Championship, ending her 18-year professional career; Nordqvist will captain Team Europe at the Solheim Cup from September 11-13, live on Sky Sports Golf Ali Stafford Senior Sports Journalist Wednesday 26 August 2026 14:56, UK Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Anna Nordqvist announced her retirement from playing professional golf with an emotional video posted on her Instagram page Solheim Cup captain Anna Nordqvist has announced via social media that she will retire from playing professional golf after this week's FM Championship, live on Sky Sports . The three-time major winner will captain Team Europe at Bernardus Golf from September 11-13, having featured in each of the previous nine Solheim Cups as a player and been part of five winning teams. Nordqvist has been a playing vice-captain in the last two contests but quickly ruled herself out of juggling captaincy with playing against Team USA in the Netherlands, despite still regularly featuring on the LPGA Tour and impressing in the majors. metadata.summary: Manchester City are considering making a bid for Chelsea midfielder Enzo Fernandez before the transfer deadline.
metadata.content: Enzo Fernandez transfer news: Man City considering bid for Chelsea midfielder | Football News | Sky Sports Skip to content Transfer Enzo Fernandez transfer news: Man City considering bid for Chelsea midfielder Enzo Fernandez joined Chelsea from Benfica for £107m in 2023; the Argentine played in Chelsea's first Premier League game of the season against Fulham; Chelsea set a deadline earlier in August for City to bid but Enzo Maresca still holds an interest in his former player By Kaveh Solhekol and Lyall Thomas Wednesday 26 August 2026 14:33, UK Image: Man City want to sign Enzo Fernandez from Chelsea Manchester City are considering making a bid for Chelsea midfielder Enzo Fernandez before the transfer deadline. Man City's interest continues despite missing Chelsea's August 14 deadline to bid for Fernandez. Chelsea spent a British-record £117m on Morgan Rogers this summer and it could take more than that for City to sign Fernandez, who is valued by the Blues at £120m after the club signed him for £107m in 2023. City are rebuilding their midfield, having sold Rodri to Barcelon a for £65.4m and Tijjani Reijnders to Al Qadsiah for £51m, after releasing Bernardo Silva , and with Nico Gonzalez set to join Newcastle for £50m. They have added Elliot Anderson from Nottingham Forest for £116m and, on Wednesday, signed Lille's Ayyoub Bouaddi for £86m. messages.text: Celtic CL post-mortem: What went wrong and where do they go from here?

metadata.summary: Celtic have spent the last couple of years making Champions League qualification look like a problem they simply cannot solve. But even by their recent standards, this was a collapse of remarkable proportions.
metadata.content: Celtic knocked out of Champions League: How will the Hoops respond to collapse in transfer window? | Football News | Sky Sports Skip to content Analysis Celtic knocked out of Champions League: How will the Hoops respond to collapse in transfer window? Celtic were on the wrong end of a historic LASK Champions League comeback to deny Martin O'Neill's side a spot in the league-phase draw; Sky Sports News' Anthony Joseph takes us through the implications after Celtic miss out on the Champions League for the second straight season Anthony Joseph News Editor @AnthonyRJoseph Wednesday 26 August 2026 14:30, UK Image: What's next for Celtic and Martin O'Neill after missing out on the Champions League? Celtic have spent the last couple of years making Champions League qualification look like a problem they simply cannot solve. But even by their recent standards, this was a collapse of remarkable proportions. Four goals ahead with less than an hour still to play across the tie, Celtic somehow found themselves on the wrong end of a 5-4 aggregate defeat to LASK. A place in the league phase was theirs to lose - and they lost it spectacularly, with individual mistakes, questionable decisions and a team that appeared to run out of answers when the pressure mounted. The fallout will inevitably focus on Martin O'Neill, who took responsibility for the defeat afterwards. But this feels like a much bigger failure than one manager or one night.
